status: Proposed visual teaching map; existing images inspected; no Godot or tutorial edits
evidence_scope: Saved museum pictures establish visible context. Dynamic behavior is described by the current route; this task did not rerun the museum. Browser diagrams are proposed teaching models, not captured runtime instrumentation.

maps.concept: Elapsed time and an if/else boundary
maps.action: Scrub elapsed seconds from before to beyond a chosen duration; then change duration with endpoints held fixed.
maps.consequence: The cube moves between two marked endpoints, reaches the finish, and stays there while the clock can continue.
maps.contrast: Before duration: moving branch. At and after duration: holding branch. Separate height, size and turn variations.
maps.observable_now: The photographed museum corridor contains the pickup cubes; the route describes linear timed demonstrations.
maps.proposed_highlight: A separate side-view cube, seconds ruler, duration marker and two branch lamps. Show elapsed as retained state and delta as one small added interval.
maps.pitfall: A still image does not show timing, branch execution or frame-rate independence. Do not depict a sine trajectory as the existing museum motion.
maps.image_caption: Saved museum capture: pickup cubes along the corridor. Time and branch indicators are proposed.

maps.concept: An event calls a reset handler
maps.action: Advance the model to mid-crossing, press Reset once, and then advance again.
maps.consequence: An event pulse reaches the reset function; elapsed returns to zero and the deck's starting pose is restored. Later frame steps continue the trip.
maps.contrast: One reset event versus repeated frame updates. A moving deck surface versus the displacement carried to a rider.
maps.observable_now: The photo shows a deck, landing and bank control with an alignment readout; it locates the physical crossing encounter.
maps.proposed_highlight: A small event-to-handler arrow beside three state boxes: elapsed, deck pose and rider position. Flash the event arrow once; animate frame pulses separately.
maps.pitfall: The photographed BANK/RESET control is not proof of the proposed learner timing-reset contract. Label the event/state schematic as a teaching proposal; rider transport remains supplied.
maps.image_caption: Saved museum capture: rotating crossing, destination and bank control.

maps.concept: Retained waypoint index and a zero-length guard
maps.action: Move a marker through a four-entry route with two equal consecutive waypoints; step once at a time.
maps.consequence: The active leg and index are highlighted. The repeated point produces a zero-length leg, whose division is skipped before the next leg becomes active.
maps.contrast: One update through time versus a loop inspecting all route entries in one call; route length versus direct endpoint separation.
maps.observable_now: The saved three-panel picture compares rail, diagonal and another route between common endpoints.
maps.proposed_highlight: Numbered route entries linked to a top-down path, current index, leg-length readout and a guard lamp. Show duplicate entries as two list slots at one spatial position.
maps.pitfall: Different drawn journeys do not establish safe zero-length handling. Keep the proposed guard display separate from the museum capture; do not skip intervening travel to make the animation simpler.
maps.image_caption: Saved comparison of three journeys; the index and guard demonstration is proposed.

maps.concept: A returning position function and order of turns
maps.action: Use the same off-axis point and two named 90-degree turns; swap their order while preserving both angles and the pivot.
maps.consequence: Two endpoint markers land at different positions, with their intermediate position visible after each first turn.
maps.contrast: Turn X then Y versus Y then X; rotating an offset around a pivot versus translating the pivot.
maps.observable_now: The photo locates the rotation study and marked angular forms; the route names the composition workbench.
maps.proposed_highlight: An isometric axis triad, one pivot, a radius line, and two colored sequential paths. Label function inputs and the returned final position.
maps.pitfall: A flat two-dimensional rotation comparison will not show general noncommutativity. Use distinct 3D axes and a nondegenerate point; some special inputs do yield equal results.
maps.image_caption: Saved museum rotation context. Ordered point paths are a proposed schematic.

maps.action: Scale a small parent group from one to two while a comparison doorway remains outside the group.
maps.consequence: The children's visible dimensions and separation double around the parent's origin, while the external doorway remains fixed.
maps.contrast: Scaling the parent versus scaling one child's own geometry; direct references still identify the same children.
maps.observable_now: The photo shows the serving/plate encounter at a changed apparent scale. The route describes the room changing around an unchanged visitor.
maps.proposed_highlight: A minimal parent-to-two-children tree paired with a front view, distance brackets and a fixed doorway silhouette. Ghost the original child positions.
maps.pitfall: A dramatic camera view alone cannot identify transform ownership, player scaling or relocation. Show the schematic ownership explicitly and keep relocation separate.
maps.image_caption: Saved scale encounter. It conveys bodily proportion; the parent/child teaching diagram is proposed.

maps.action: Move a visitor marker near, away, and near again, then press Reset.
maps.consequence: The current-near lamp follows distance immediately; the remembered-visit lamp remains on after departure until reset. A reversible block and retained opening respond differently.
maps.contrast: A value recomputed from the present input versus a value retained from an earlier event.
maps.observable_now: The saved before/after comparison shows a cut remaining in the lattice after the body has left; a separate route image shows nearby slats.
maps.proposed_highlight: A distance threshold ring, two explicitly named lamps and a short near/away timeline. Keep the remembered flag's history visible after the visitor leaves.
maps.pitfall: A retained opening does not expose the actual internal variable or prove it is implemented as this boolean. Label the two-flag model as a reduced teaching representation.
maps.image_caption: Saved museum comparison: an opening remains after passage.

maps.concept: Compose familiar rules through one shared input
maps.action: Choose an opening fraction and hold it at a middle value; then let a supplied occupancy input request opening or closing.
maps.consequence: Two leaves change position, angle and size together; a visible gap can be compared with a fixed body-width marker.
maps.contrast: One shared fraction driving several functions versus unrelated values that can disagree. Reset restores the chosen starting state.
maps.observable_now: The photo compares two timed sizes in the level-ground room; the route describes the airlock and composed transformations.
maps.proposed_highlight: A top-down pair of leaves, a single fraction slider feeding three labeled outputs, and a clearance bracket at the narrowest shown gap.
maps.pitfall: The screenshot is of a growing obstacle, not proof of the proposed two-leaf learner model. Browser clearance is a geometric illustration and does not verify Godot collision or headset passage.
maps.image_caption: Saved timed-room comparison. The shared-fraction airlock diagram is proposed.

maps.concept: Slots, object references and independent objects
maps.action: Select a stored reference and move its target; switch between two references to one object and references to two separately created objects. Separately empty one occupancy slot.
maps.consequence: Reference arrows identify the target whose position changes. Two aliases still end at one object; independent references end at distinct objects. An emptied occupancy address stays in place.
maps.contrast: One object with two names versus two objects; stored occupancy versus the visible object and its reference.
maps.observable_now: The photo shows a row, grid and related museum exhibits. Collections and spatial repetition are visible.
maps.proposed_highlight: A separated data strip and scene strip joined by arrows; show alias and independent cases side by side, plus a retained empty slot with its unchanged index.
maps.pitfall: Neither repeated cubes nor a screenshot proves identity or memory aliasing. The arrows and reference experiment are proposed teaching views, not extracted live Godot memory.
maps.image_caption: Saved museum array hall. Reference ownership is made visible only in the proposed diagram.

maps.action: Choose the unequal coordinate x=1, y=2, z=3 in the four-by-four-by-four volume, then write one value and read it back.
maps.consequence: One cube highlights in space while its storage trail opens as values[2][3][1]. Neighbouring cells retain their values.
maps.contrast: Displayed [x,y,z] versus stored [y][z][x]; changing spacing changes physical positions without changing addresses.
maps.observable_now: The photo clearly shows indexed cubes within the flight volume, including [2,2,2] and [2,2,3].
maps.proposed_highlight: An exploded layer view, three color-consistent axes and a breadcrumb from y-layer to z-row to x-entry. Use unequal indices in the proposed selection.
maps.pitfall: Equal indices can conceal a swapped-axis error. An extra index supplies an address, not flight; flight controls and row/layer construction remain supplied or explicitly explained.
maps.image_caption: Saved labeled volume; proposed layer view explains the storage convention.

maps.concept: A repeating address-to-turn rule with one exception
maps.action: Select an address in a four-by-four field, predict its quarter-turn from the displayed remainder rule, then set one exceptional address.
maps.consequence: The selected asymmetric motif rotates; expanding the field extends the same rule while preserving the named exception.
maps.contrast: Zero as a valid orientation versus zero as empty occupancy; changing the rule versus replacing the motif.
maps.observable_now: The saved overhead picture shows six differently organized fields made from a related motif vocabulary.
maps.proposed_highlight: An address grid beside an enlarged motif, a numeric remainder wheel 0-3, and one outlined exception. Use a deterministic rule such as (x+z)%4.
maps.pitfall: The installed fields are raster images. Draw cell outlines as a browser explanation, not as evidence of per-tile nodes, collision bodies or stored occupancy.
maps.image_caption: Saved six-field museum comparison; the selected address and remainder wheel are proposed.

maps.action: First rotate the pattern inside a fixed wall; then rotate the wall carrying the unchanged pattern.
maps.consequence: Pattern orientation changes in the first comparison while the wall outline stays fixed. In the second, wall outline and passage direction change together.
maps.contrast: Image coordinates versus the transform of the physical carrier; shared source versus apparent size at different viewing distances.
maps.observable_now: The photo shows upright patterned surfaces with a marked exception and a wall opening/context.
maps.proposed_highlight: Two small top views with separate texture-arrow and wall-outline indicators. Keep the same source-image swatch visible beside both.
maps.pitfall: A photograph cannot prove shared image identity or collision motion. The existing floor/wall generator does not automatically transfer a learner's edited image; that assignment remains explicit and proposed.
maps.image_caption: Saved patterned-wall encounter; source and carrier indicators are proposed.

maps.concept: A retained boolean score read by a clock
maps.action: Toggle one step in a short score and advance the playhead; then change tempo without changing any stored steps.
maps.consequence: The playhead visits each address. True entries emit a momentary trigger pulse; false entries emit none. Tempo changes the spacing of visits while the score remains.
maps.contrast: Stored score versus present playhead versus triggered event; a false entry means no new trigger, not stop an already ringing sound.
maps.observable_now: The saved image shows a lit strip in the museum floor. The route separately identifies a sequencer and independently changing floor.
maps.proposed_highlight: A clearly separate eight-step browser score, moving cursor, trigger lamp and event timeline. A play/step/reset control can expose retained index and elapsed time.
maps.pitfall: Do not infer sequencer state from the floor screenshot, call its lit strip a recorded score, or imply footsteps recorded it. The proposed eight-step diagram is smaller than the installed four-track, sixteen-step instrument; its twelve-column floor is not the score.
maps.image_caption: Saved museum floor only. The independent score/playhead diagram is proposed.
